purpose: Formatting-only normalization of brand strings before comparison. This ontology deliberately contains NO brand alias table.

sources.role: production brand provenance vocabulary: visual | visible_text | logo_shape | catalog_corroboration | commerce_corroboration | unknown

normalizationSteps.name: collapse_whitespace
normalizationSteps.rule: Collapse internal whitespace runs to a single space.

normalizationSteps.name: case_fold
normalizationSteps.rule: Lowercase for comparison. The original casing is preserved for reporting.

normalizationSteps.name: strip_trademark_symbols
normalizationSteps.rule: Remove ® ™ © ℗ and the ASCII sequences (r) (tm) (c) when they appear as trailing or standalone marks.

normalizationSteps.name: strip_punctuation
normalizationSteps.rule: Remove . , ' ’ ´ ` and collapse - and & to a single space. Applied to BOTH sides symmetrically.

normalizationSteps.name: strip_legal_suffix
normalizationSteps.rule: Remove a TRAILING legal-entity suffix from the verified list below, and only when it is the final token.

verifiedLegalSuffixes._comment: Generic corporate-form suffixes only. Each is a legal entity marker, never a distinguishing part of a fashion brand name.
verifiedLegalSuffixes.appliedOnlyWhen: the suffix is the LAST token AND at least one token remains after removal
verifiedLegalSuffixes.rationale: 'Gucci' and 'Guccio Gucci S.p.A.' are the same legal brand. Stripping a trailing S.p.A. is a formatting normalization, not a merge of two brands.

prohibitedOperations.rule: FORBIDDEN. Two brands are never merged because their names look similar, share a prefix, or have a small edit distance.
prohibitedOperations.note: Several of these pairs ARE related in the real world as parent brand and diffusion line. That relationship is a business fact, not a formatting difference, and asserting it requires evidence this ontology does not have. They are scored as distinct until an owner-approved alias table exists.

prohibitedOperations.rule: FORBIDDEN. No brand alias may be added without documented evidence. This file intentionally ships an EMPTY alias table.
FORBIDDEN. A leading 'the' is NOT stripped. 'The North Face' and 'North Face' remain distinct strings, because stripping the article is a name change, not punctuation.
NOT APPLIED in v1. Folding é -> e would silently merge names that differ meaningfully in some scripts. Recorded as an open question rather than applied.

aliasTable._comment: INTENTIONALLY EMPTY. Populating this requires per-entry documented evidence (official corporate disclosure or verified product record) and owner approval. An empty table is the correct fail-safe: it can only cause a true match to be scored as a miss, never a false brand match to be scored as correct.

evidenceRequirement._comment: Brand GROUND TRUTH admissibility. Mirrors the Phase 0B labeling standard.
acceptable: visible brand label or care tag in the image
evidenceRequirement.productionAlignment: The production brand provenance vocabulary distinguishes visible_text and logo_shape (direct evidence) from visual (inference). Only direct-evidence provenances correspond to admissible ground truth. Note that production DOES emit provenance 'visual' for a pure brand_guess, so a prediction carrying provenance 'visual' is an inference the evaluation treats as an unsupported claim when ground truth is not_visible or unknown.

scoringNotes.nullPreference: Brand strongly prefers null/unknown over a guess. A null brand prediction against a known brand label is unknown_when_evidence_exists (moderate penalty). A wrong or invented brand against a not_visible/unknown label is unsupported_certainty (highest penalty).
scoringNotes.caseInsensitive: Comparison is case-insensitive after normalization. 'GUCCI', 'Gucci', and 'gucci' are one brand.
